topic_development_chronological.development: User asked for a step-by-step guide to import DEEP-VOICE (Kaggle, birdy654/deep-voice-deepfake-voice-recognition) and the Gary Stafford dataset (confirmed via web search to be garystafford/deepfake-audio-detection on Hugging Face — 1,866 clips, 933 real/933 synthetic, English, 6 TTS platforms) and prepare both for downstream preprocessing, specific to VS Code on Windows and project name 'morph'.
topic_development_chronological.delivered: A 6-phase plan: (0) prerequisites, (1) project skeleton (data/raw/{deep_voice,gary_stafford}, data/interim, data/metadata, scripts/), (2) venv + requirements.txt, (3) Kaggle CLI download + organize_deep_voice.py to flatten into real/fake folders, (4) HF datasets load_dataset + export_gary_stafford.py to write WAV files into matching real/fake folders, (5) audit_datasets.py using soundfile to catch corrupt files and log duration/sample_rate/channels per source+label, (6) build_metadata.py to produce data/metadata/master_metadata.csv with bonafide/spoof labels (ASVspoof-convention naming, chosen deliberately for forward compatibility with the planned future ASVspoof 2019 LA integration).

topic_development_chronological.development: Flagged, unprompted, that DEEP-VOICE's very small/narrow speaker set (RVC impersonations of only a couple of public figures) makes a genuine speaker-disjoint split within DEEP-VOICE alone meaningless — speaker-disjointness will have to come primarily from Gary Stafford's broader speaker pool and later ASVspoof 2019 LA, not from DEEP-VOICE.

User ran the Phase 4 inspection script (load_dataset + print(ds['train'][0])) and hit: `ImportError: To support decoding audio data, please install 'torchcodec'.` This occurred because the datasets library's default Audio feature tries to auto-decode via torchcodec, which wasn't installed and would otherwise require matching torch + system ffmpeg versions on Windows — assessed as more setup friction than warranted at this stage.

Root cause explained (torchcodec decoder dependency) and fix provided: `ds.cast_column("audio", Audio(decode=False))` to stop automatic decoding, then manually decode raw bytes via `soundfile.read(io.BytesIO(raw_bytes))` inside a rewritten export_gary_stafford.py, with a fallback suggestion (librosa.load via audioread) if libsndfile lacks MP3 support for any clips.
topic_development_chronological.status: User did not report back on the export script's failed/succeeded count explicitly, but the fact that Phase 5's audit shows gary_stafford at 933/933 with corrupt=0 for both classes implies the export completed cleanly for all 1,866 clips.

topic_development_chronological.topic: Phase 5 audit results reported by user
topic_development_chronological.development:
User ran audit_datasets.py and pasted the summary table:

| source | label | count | corrupt | mean_duration | sample_rates |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| deep_voice | fake | 56 | 0 | 467.94s | [40000, 44100] |
| deep_voice | real | 8 | 0 | 468.09s | [44100, 48000] |
| gary_stafford | fake | 933 | 0 | 3.68s | [16000] |
| gary_stafford | real | 933 | 0 | 4.72s | [44100] |

No corrupt files in either dataset — integrity gate passed cleanly. User then explicitly said they are stopping here and will continue from later, and requested this handoff JSON immediately after pasting the audit output — no further phases (6+) have been run or discussed yet.

critical_findings_from_audit_not_yet_act.finding: DEEP-VOICE clip counts are very small and severely imbalanced: only 56 fake vs 8 real (64 total files), with mean durations around 468 seconds (~7.8 minutes) per file — these are long-form clips, not short utterances like gary_stafford's ~3.7-4.7s clips. This is a structurally different data shape from gary_stafford and will need explicit handling (e.g. chunking into shorter windows) before it can be merged into a unified feature-extraction pipeline.
critical_findings_from_audit_not_yet_act.severity: high — both the extreme class imbalance (8 real files) and the long-form-vs-short-form mismatch with gary_stafford need a stated plan before Phase 6/feature extraction.

critical_findings_from_audit_not_yet_act.finding: Sample-rate/label confound inside gary_stafford: ALL real clips are 44100 Hz and ALL fake clips are 16000 Hz — the label is perfectly correlated with sample rate within this dataset. If features are extracted without first resampling everything to a common rate, a classifier could trivially learn to distinguish real/fake by sample-rate artifacts (e.g. upsampling/interpolation signatures) rather than genuine spoofing cues — this would produce misleadingly high accuracy that fails to generalize.
critical_findings_from_audit_not_yet_act.status: unaddressed — this is the single most important open issue for the next session
critical_findings_from_audit_not_yet_act.severity: critical — this is exactly the kind of 'model/data mismatch' false-positive-cause category previously flagged in this user's broader project work (SentinelVoice), and the same rigor standard applies here: this must be fixed (resample everything to one target rate, e.g. 16kHz, as a mandatory step before feature extraction) and the fix should be explicitly justified/documented, not just applied silently.

critical_findings_from_audit_not_yet_act.finding: DEEP-VOICE also has mixed sample rates across and within classes (40000/44100 for fake, 44100/48000 for real) — another resampling-before-features requirement, compounding the same confound risk at smaller scale.
